canonical_question: Is the 62 at% Cr and 30 at% V composition inside the Cr-V-rich phase a steady-state equilibrium value or a snapshot dependent on the 1000 K simulation duration?

question_variants.question: Is the 62 at% Cr and 30 at% V composition inside the Cr-V-rich phase a steady-state equilibrium value or a snapshot dependent on the 1000 K simulation duration?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states the composition inside the Cr-V-rich phase is 62 at% Cr and 30 at% V as a result of the CMC simulation at 1000 K. It suggests the difference between simulation and experiment (steady-state vs. irradiation-modified) is a kinetic effect, implying the simulation value represents the thermodynamic equilibrium or steady-state of the simulation conditions rather than a transient snapshot.

answers.answer: The composition inside the Cr-V–rich phase is found to be 62 at % Cr and 30 at % V in the simulation. The paper attributes differences in composition between simulation and experiment to kinetic effects, implying the simulation value reflects the steady-state microstructure under the simulated irradiation conditions or equilibrium at the simulation temperature.
answers.measurement_outcome: 62 at% Cr, 30 at% V, 5 at% W, 3 at% Ta
answers.mechanism: Kinetic effect of irradiation modifying steady-state microstructure
answers.boundary_limitation: Simulations represent thermodynamic equilibrium, irradiation creates non-steady-state
evidence_spans: we have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature.
The enthalpies of mixing were calculated using the density functional theory (DFT) and CE methods for nearly 270 structures within the BCC underlying crystalline lattice.

In agreement with previous DFT/CE studies for W-Ta and W-V systems ( [33] ), it is found that the enthalpies of mixing for these two binaries are negative for the whole compositional range, a trend followed also by the Cr-V binary.
